rationale: Matthew 10:1-4 names "His twelve disciples" and "the twelve apostles" but does not mention the tribes. Genesis 49:28 closes Jacob's blessings with "These are the tribes of Israel, twelve in all" (BSB). The link between the two twelves is not this lesson's inference. Matthew makes it himself later: "you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel" (19:28, BSB; also Luke 22:30). Revelation 21:12-14 puts both sets of names on one city, "the names of the twelve tribes of Israel" on its gates and "the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb" on its foundations. Acts 1:26 restores the number after Judas, when Matthias is "added to the eleven apostles". E. P. Sanders (Jesus and Judaism, 1985, pp. 326-327, read through a website's reproduction) lists "the call of the twelve" among the key facts for what he calls "Jewish restoration eschatology". Graded motif because what is traced is a recurring number and pattern, not quoted wording. The label is strong because the New Testament itself pairs the Twelve with the twelve tribes and a named scholar argues the point. What the pairing means is not decided here. Readers differ on whether it signals a restored Israel, a renewed people that includes Gentiles, or something else, and this app's own lens offers twelve tribes and twelve apostles only as a parallel to test.
